speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with feeding intolerance and bilious vomiting; this is a serious symptom that requires immediate investigation. To begin my assessment, can you tell me exactly when these symptoms started and have you noticed any specific abdominal swelling or color changes?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, 3050-g (6-lb 12-oz) male, six hours post delivery. The newborn has had several episodes of bilious vomiting and is intolerant to feeding since birth. Was born at term following an uncomplicated pregnancy, though the mother missed several prenatal checkups. The patient's older brother underwent surgery for pyloric stenosis as an infant.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Intestinal Malrotation with Volvulus.

The onset of bilious vomiting within six hours of birth, combined with a family history of pyloric stenosis and maternal lack of prenatal care, strongly suggests a congenital anomaly. I am requesting an urgent Abdominal Ultrasound and X-Ray to confirm the diagnosis.
